name: ropensci/skynet
what_it_holds: Peer-reviewed rOpenSci R package with import_db1b() and import_t100() functions that parse raw BTS DB1B (Coupon/Ticket) and T-100 segment CSVs downloaded from transtats.bts.gov into tidy data frames, plus make_net_dir() to build directed air-transport networks (city-pair traffic, fares) with statistical edge filtering. Includes a convert_raw() helper to compress raw files to needed variables. Topics tagged: bts, transtats, rita, t100, db1b, bureau-of-transport-statistics. Does not fetch On-Time Performance data. No raw data committed (BYO download from BTS website); this is a tidying/network-construction method, not a stored dataset.
why_useful: Directly targets gap #10 (airline capacity/traffic as a travel-demand kernel analogue for ABNB nights) — a maintained, peer-reviewed method for turning raw BTS T-100 (city-pair capacity/seats/departures) and DB1B (fare/itinerary) files into usable panels, saving the team from writing a T-100/DB1B parser from scratch.
geography: US domestic + international segments touching the US (BTS scope)
time_coverage: Whatever vintage of T-100/DB1B the user downloads from BTS (historical archive back to 1990s available at source)
size_hint: Method only, no committed data; T-100/DB1B source files are large (DB1B ~GB-scale per quarter)
license: rOpenSci package, GPL-family typical (license file present, not read in full)
last_activity: Last updated 2024-09-12 per GitHub topic page
themes: US air travel: BTS T-100 segment, DB1B fares, Form 41, on-time performance; repos that download and tidy them; TSA throughput scrapers
Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: Directly targets gap #10 (airline capacity/traffic as a travel-demand kernel analogue for ABNB nights) — a maintained, peer-reviewed method for turning raw BTS T-100 (city-pair capacity/seats/departures) and DB1B (fare/itinerary) files into usable panels, saving the team from writing a T-100/DB1B parser from scratch.

T-100 is the closest thing to genuine 'airline seat capacity by route' public data (monthly, by carrier, domestic+international, free from BTS); this package is a ready-made, tested pipeline for turning it into route-network capacity series that could proxy inbound/outbound travel capacity to Airbnb-relevant markets (esp. US gateway cities, and international routes feeding APAC/LatAm markets).

DB1B/T-100 are the exact 'airline capacity and traffic' data named in gap 10; this is a maintained, peer-reviewed one-command pull method for a large, free, official US domestic fare/traffic dataset spanning 1990s-present, directly usable as a travel-volume/pricing proxy.

DB1B/T100 is the authoritative US domestic airfare + passenger-volume + route-network dataset (gap 10: airline capacity/traffic) and could proxy long-haul/US travel demand and average realized fares by O&D market as a consumer-travel-spend cross-check; this package removes most of the BTS data-wrangling pain.

name: OpenSky Network COVID-19 flight dataset
what_it_holds: Daily global flight-level records (callsign, ICAO24, origin/destination airport where inferable, first/last-seen times, altitude profile) crowdsourced from 2,500+ ADS-B ground receivers, published by the OpenSky Network / Eurocontrol PRU academic team, coverage from 1 Jan 2019 to present, updated continuously; documented in Strohmeier et al. 2021, Earth System Science Data, DOI 10.5194/essd-13-357-2021. Not a GitHub-committed dataset -- served via an S3-style bucket browser at opensky-network.org, free for research use with attribution. GitHub repos that consume it (e.g. siddharth271101/Covid-19-and-Aviation-Industry, a Spark/EMR pipeline joining it to JHU CSSE COVID case counts, MIT licence, 29 commits) show the pull method.
why_useful: This is essentially a global daily flight-volume series since 2019 -- a genuine travel-demand proxy usable for gap #10 (airline/rail/road capacity and traffic) and cross-checkable against nights/ADR seasonality and COVID-era base effects; far larger and more current than TSA throughput (already tried and found weak since 2024) because it is global, not US-security-line-only.
size_hint: multi-TB raw, but aggregatable to daily flight counts per country/airport; ~7 years of daily data
license: free for research/education with attribution; not a standard OSS licence
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: This is essentially a global daily flight-volume series since 2019 -- a genuine travel-demand proxy usable for gap #10 (airline/rail/road capacity and traffic) and cross-checkable against nights/ADR seasonality and COVID-era base effects; far larger and more current than TSA throughput (already tried and found weak since 2024) because it is global, not US-security-line-only.
